story: On this breezy, clear Wednesday morning in Sumter Oaks, Gary is at his workbench at home, carefully wiring an LED strip and speaker mount and testing the connections quietly. Across the way, Donna is packing paddles, balls, water, and a knee strap for Gary, determined to make their ten o'clock pickleball session. Over at his house, Hal is methodically reviewing his logged cart measurements and flamingo count, double-checking every figure in his violation notebook. Meanwhile, Rosa is at her dining table counting chairs and plates for four guests and sketching out her optimistic plans for Friday.
events: Gary (gary workbench): Finish wiring the LED strip and speaker mount, test the connections quietly
Donna (donna pickleball bag): Pack paddles, balls, water, and a knee strap for Gary before our ten o'clock session
Hal (hal violation notebook): Review the logged cart measurements and flamingo count, correct any errors
Rosa (rosa dining table): Check the table, count chairs and plates for four guests, and plan the setup for Friday

gary.thought_process: I'm back home at my workbench with no one around, so this is a good hour to keep building. The LED strip and speaker mount are partly wired from last tick, and I've been keeping everything quiet in the garage until the Architectural Review approval comes through on the filing, since L-01 covers exterior mods visible from the street and L-03 rules out amplified sound at night. Nothing blasting, just careful wiring and testing the connections. Donna would get a kick out of seeing the finished cart, and keeping my hands busy beats sitting around the quiet house.

parameters.content: Finish wiring the LED strip and speaker mount, test the connections quietly

donna.thought_process: Gary and I agreed on ten o'clock at the courts this morning, and it's already past eight. Last tick I checked the calendar and wanted a two-hour slot, which is the L-05 maximum. Hal also mentioned the flamingos, so I'll need to trim down to three before Friday dinner. First things first: my pickleball bag is right here, so I'll pack it with paddles, balls, and a knee strap for Gary so we're ready to go at ten.

parameters.content: Pack paddles, balls, water, and a knee strap for Gary before our ten o'clock session

hal.thought_process: I'm at home, nobody in sight, and I've already measured Gary's cart and logged the notes. Gary just showed up on Magnolia Loop last tick. The notebook is right here, and I want the record accurate before the review committee sees anything. A last look at the entries is sensible, and then I'll step out and see what's actually visible from the street. Gary's form is nearly ready, so I'd rather the facts be right than anyone get surprised on Tuesday.

parameters.content: Review the logged cart measurements and flamingo count, correct any errors

rosa.thought_process: I've already posted the invite, checked the pantry, and written the shopping list, and I looked at my shift schedule to confirm Friday afternoon is free. Donna, Gary, and Hal have all said yes, so there's no need to chase anyone. The next real step is getting the ingredients. The dining table is where this whole thing comes together, so I'll take stock of it now: count seats and figure out whether four chairs and my good plates are enough, then head out for groceries. Better to settle the table now than scramble Friday afternoon.

parameters.content: Check the table, count chairs and plates for four guests, and plan the setup for Friday

laws.title: Cart Modifications
laws.text: Exterior golf cart modifications visible from the street require Architectural Review approval.

laws.title: Lawn Ornaments
laws.text: No more than 3 decorative ornaments may be visible from the street.

laws.title: Quiet Hours
laws.text: No amplified sound from 10 PM to 7 AM.

laws.title: Holiday Decor
laws.text: Holiday lighting is permitted from Thanksgiving through January 15.

laws.title: Court Reservations
laws.text: Pickleball courts may be reserved for a maximum of 2 hours per party.

laws.title: Parking
laws.text: No parking on the grass. Carts and cars stay on driveways or the street.
